appearance_facts.fact: The chart title is 'Monthly Sales for Store B in City Y'.
The vertical axis is labeled 'Sales ($K)' with tick marks from 0 to 500 in increments of 50.
The horizontal axis is labeled 'Month' with tick marks for 'April', 'May', and 'June'.
A red dashed horizontal line is labeled 'Average' and is positioned at the 250 ($K) mark on the vertical axis.
The bar for April is orange and its top is at the 250 ($K) level, exactly on the 'Average' line.
The bar for May is orange and its top is at the 450 ($K) level, above the 'Average' line.
The bar for June is orange and its top is at the 350 ($K) level, above the 'Average' line.
The chart is titled 'Monthly Sales for Store B in City Y'.

public_definitions: The user's goal is to review the Store B monthly sales dashboard for April through June, then choose the April route in the monthly sales operations form.
The primary field label is 'April sales route'.
The options for the April sales route are: 'Route April to low-sales response', 'Keep April on normal sales monitoring', 'Route April to strong-sales response'.

The companion fields include 'Store unit', 'Review month', 'Sales record', and 'Operations program', all of which are set to 'Store B', 'April', 'Monthly sales', and 'Monthly sales status routing', respectively.
uncertain: The exact sales value for April is not explicitly labeled on the chart, only its position relative to the 'Average' line.
